story: Buffalo City Hall is a 32-story Art Deco skyscraper at 65 Niagara Square. It is 398 feet tall and was completed on November 10, 1931. It was dedicated on July 1, 1932, to mark the city's Centennial.

The building cost $6,851,546.85 including the architect's fees, which made it one of the costliest city halls in the country. It has 1,520 windows on the first 25 floors, and all of them open inward, so there is no need for window washers outside.

The architects were Dietel, Wade & Jones. The friezes were sculpted by Albert Stewart and carried out by Rene Paul Chambellan. Near the top are polychrome terra cotta chevrons, and the walls are covered in Ohio sandstone and gray Minnesota limestone.
stops.disputed: Many people think the style is simply Art Deco. Wikipedia says architect John Wade called it "Americanesque" and sometimes Babylonian.

story: The Ellicott Square Building was designed by Charles Atwood of D. H. Burnham & Company, and finished in May 1896. It was built in less than a year for $3.5 million.

It had 10 stories and 447,000 square feet, which made it the largest office building in the world by floor area until 1908. Daniel Burnham's mantra was "make no little plans." The building is named after Joseph Ellicott, who laid out Buffalo.

Inside is a courtyard with a glass roof and a marble mosaic floor with 23 million pieces of marble, showing sun symbols from civilizations around the world. In 1896 and 1897 the building also housed the Vitascope Theater.
stops.disputed: Many people think a movie theater of this age was in New York or Paris. Wikipedia says the earliest known dedicated motion picture theater in the world was here in Buffalo.

claims.t: It was the tallest building in the world.
claims.why: It was the largest by floor area, not the tallest.

story: The Old Post Office is at 121 Ellicott Street. The Office of the Supervising Architect, with Jeremiah O'Rourke, designed it, and construction started in 1897. It opened in 1901 and cost $1.5 million.

It was Buffalo's central post office until 1963, and it was the tallest building in the city from 1901 to 1912. Wikipedia describes it as a four-story Gothic Revival building with a 244-foot tower over the central entrance and a roofed courtyard.
After the post office moved out, federal offices used the building. Since 1981 it has been home to the city campus of Erie Community College.
stops.disputed: Many people think a post office is a small building. Wikipedia says this one was the tallest in the city for 11 years.

claims.t: The Old Post Office opened in 1901.
It has been a college since the 1930s.

story: The Buffalo History Museum building was built in 1901 as the New York State pavilion for the Pan-American Exposition. It is the only permanent structure from the Exposition that still stands. George Cary, a Buffalo architect, designed it.
Its south portico is meant to evoke the Parthenon in Athens. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1980 and designated a National Historic Landmark in 1987.

The society was founded in 1862, and its first president was Millard Fillmore. It has hosted observances of Lincoln's Birthday for over a century. In 1960 the name changed to the Buffalo and Erie County Historical Society, and it is now the Buffalo History Museum.
stops.fact: It is the Expo's only survivor.
stops.disputed: Many people think the whole Pan-American Exposition is long gone. Wikipedia says this building is the one permanent structure that survives.
